tutorial.title: Quick Guide
tutorial.mission: Mission: follow the yellow targets, revisit all three fixed stations, and record three kinds of marine life.
tutorial.moveMission: Swim to the bright yellow target to find the next fixed station.
tutorial.interactMission: When you are close to a fixed station, press E to open the viewfinder.
tutorial.photoMission: Press SPACE in the viewfinder or near marine life to save photo evidence.
tutorial.move: Move: WASD / arrow keys, or drag on touch.
tutorial.explore: Find a fixed survey station. Press E to enter the viewfinder, then SPACE to take the photo.
tutorial.oxygen: The tank bar shows your safe dive time. At zero, the vessel returns you safely.
tutorial.tools: Your survey unit quietly saves nearby water and habitat clues. SPACE is still required to photograph evidence.
tutorial.evidence: Photos are evidence: compare the earlier view with today's view.

dive.objectivePhotoInstruction: Find a station · E enters the viewfinder · SPACE takes the photo
dive.objectiveStationInstruction: Enter the yellow ring, press E to open the viewfinder, match the old viewpoint, then press SPACE to save the station photo (+1 photo)
dive.controlsPersistent: WASD / arrows to swim  ·  follow the yellow ring  ·  E interact  ·  SPACE photograph
dive.objectiveOrganismInstruction: Move near an organism and press SPACE to record it (+1 organism) for the food-web investigation
dive.objectiveDoInstruction: Move near a fixed station; the survey unit automatically saves water, depth and habitat clues
dive.objectiveReturnInstruction: Return to the vessel · SPACE reviews the evidence
dive.observePrompt: Move close · stop · press SPACE to record a photograph
dive.stationPhotoPrompt: Press E to frame the old viewpoint, then press SPACE to save the station photo
dive.organismPhotoPrompt: Move close to the organism, then press SPACE to photograph it
dive.viewfinderCompareHint: Match the habitat and the subject before you press the shutter.
dive.observationLockedHint: This link will unlock after another species is observed.
dive.observationCaution: One encounter is a clue about this place and time, not proof of a whole-bay trend.
dive.observationReviewHint: press I to review its field notes again
dive.viewfinderControls: WASD / arrows aim the frame · SPACE shutter · E / ESC exit
dive.viewfinderNoTarget: Move closer to an unphotographed fixed station first
dive.viewfinderQualityExcellent: Framing strong: this view is ready to compare
dive.viewfinderQualityGood: Framing usable: the view can still be compared
dive.viewfinderQualityFair: Framing is wide: move closer for a clearer comparison
dive.returnReady: Evidence complete · press SPACE at the vessel to return
dive.returnIncomplete: Return to the vessel after the field notes are complete
dive.observeHint: Move closer to a subject or historical station
dive.openingToolsTitle: The diver carries a camera and a survey unit.
dive.openingToolsBody: Use the camera to photograph each fixed station and nearby marine life. The survey unit quietly saves water, depth and habitat clues in the background.
dive.openingEvidenceTitle: Bring evidence back before explaining the cause.
dive.openingEvidenceBody: A changed scene is a clue, not the answer. Photograph all three fixed stations, record three marine organisms and bring the saved water clue back to the vessel.
dive.openingEvidenceCaution: Presence, absence, and distribution shifts are clues about this survey—not proof of extinction or a single cause.
dive.briefingTitle: A change is visible. The cause is not.
dive.briefingBody: A former surveyor left three historical photographs. Return to the same locations and photograph the bay today so we can test whether it really changed.
dive.briefingQuestion: Do not guess the cause yet. Bring comparable evidence back to the vessel first.
dive.briefingKit:
1 Compare three old photos
2 Return to the same places and photograph them today
3 Record nearby marine life
4 Bring the clues back to the vessel
dive.demoFirstStep: First step: follow the yellow target to the bay entrance. The viewfinder will name the subject you need to photograph.
dive.missionBriefTitle: Today's mission: bring back comparable ocean evidence
dive.missionBriefBody: Return to three fixed observation points and photograph today's view. Record the requested marine organisms, let the survey unit save a water clue, then return to the research vessel.
dive.missionBriefStation:
Station photographs 0 / 3
Enter a yellow ring, press E for the viewfinder, then press SPACE to photograph.
dive.missionBriefSpecies:
Organism records 0 / 3
Approach the softly highlighted organism and press SPACE to photograph it.
dive.missionBriefDevice:
Water clue 0 / 1
The survey unit saves data automatically near an observation point.
dive.missionBriefReturn:
Return when complete
When the vessel gains a soft gold marker, return and press SPACE.
dive.missionBriefHint: In-game prompts keep showing the next station, requested organism, and return cue.
dive.viewfinderMission: PHOTO MISSION: frame {species} in the viewfinder
dive.briefingNote: All sites and readings in this prototype are fictional educational simulations.
dive.safeReturn: Your tank oxygen ran out. The vessel brings you back safely. This is a safety limit, not a research conclusion. Your photo evidence is incomplete, so try the route again.
dive.oxygenNotice70: Tank oxygen is about 70%. Continue to the nearest survey station.
dive.oxygenNotice40: Tank oxygen is falling. Finish the nearest station, then prepare to return.
dive.oxygenNotice20: Tank oxygen is low. Return to the research vessel now.
report.title: Evidence room
report.subtitle: You confirmed a change, but one survey cannot prove the cause.
report.photoEvidence: Earlier and current views can be compared
report.doEvidence: The survey unit saved a water-and-habitat clue
report.foodWebHint: Arrows show possible feeding links. A missing node is not proof of extinction.
report.puzzleHint: Each piece reflects this survey only: photographed, observed, or not observed here.
report.foodWebDragHint: Drag each surveyed organism into its ecological role. Arrows show possible energy and nutrient pathways, not causation proven by one visit.
report.foodWebTray: SURVEY CARDS · DRAG INTO THE ROLE ZONES
report.foodWebWrongZone: That role does not fit this organism. Try another zone.
report.foodLessonTitle: First, learn how to read a food chain
report.foodLessonDefinition: A food chain shows how energy passes between living things. The arrow points from food to the organism that eats it.
report.foodLessonExample: Seagrass  →  Small fish  →  Large reef fish
report.foodLessonWeb: Many connected food chains form a food web. Now place each survey card in the correct role.
report.notCause: The observations do not prove one cause
report.singleReading: One reading cannot represent every time, place, or depth
report.nextStep: A longer, distributed monitoring plan is needed
report.callout:
A changed image is evidence, not a cause.
We still need to find what changed in the water.
report.note: Next: follow the breathing clue and decide what must be measured over time.
report.recapStart: Finish the food web, then take the quick recap
report.recap.q1: Can one afternoon DO reading tell us whether low oxygen occurred before dawn?
report.recap.q1b: No, we need measurements over time
report.recap.q2: If surface DO is normal, must near-bed DO also be normal?
report.recap.q2a: Yes, all depths are the same
report.recap.q3: There are fewer fish today. Does that prove low oxygen is the only cause?
report.recap.q3a: No; it is evidence of change, while low oxygen is a hypothesis to test
report.recap.q3b: Yes; fewer fish can only mean low oxygen
report.recapCorrect: Correct! That is the monitoring problem for the next chapter.
report.recapTryAgain: Think again: can one photo or reading represent every time, place and depth?
report.doBridgeDefinition: Dissolved oxygen is oxygen in water that fish and many aquatic organisms can breathe. From here on, we use the abbreviation DO.
report.doBridgeWater: Oxygen in water: for fish and other aquatic life
report.doBridgeLow: Low DO: aquatic life may lack oxygen
report.doBridgeProblem: PROBLEM — A photo shows one moment, and one reading may miss low oxygen near the seabed before dawn.
report.doBridgeSolution: THEREFORE — Monitor continuously at multiple locations and depths.
opening.photoFindOneBeforeNext: Select one glowing clue in the photo and read its note before moving on.
opening.photoReviewAllBeforeConclusion: Review all three locations and log one glowing clue on each photograph first.
opening.photoConclusionTitle: Combine the clues from the archive
opening.photoConclusionQuestion: What did the historical photographs record at all three locations?
opening.photoConclusionA: More fish or groups of fish were visible at all three locations
opening.photoConclusionB: No fish were visible at any of the three locations
opening.photoConclusionCorrect: Conclusion: the earlier survey recorded more fish or fish groups at all three locations. This is the baseline for today's repeat photographs.
opening.photoConclusionTryAgain: Look again: every historical photograph includes several fish or a group of fish.
opening.photoReviewHint: Review the three fixed viewpoints before returning to the same locations.
opening.photoMeta.s1: Bay entrance · teaching simulation archive · mid-water | Focus: fish groups and habitat
opening.photoMeta.s2: Raft edge · teaching simulation archive · net cage | Focus: raft structure and fish
opening.photoMeta.s3: Inner bay · teaching simulation archive · near seabed | Focus: seabed and benthic life
opening.photoInspectHint: Hold and drag the photo to inspect it from every angle · wheel to zoom · left/right arrows switch photos
opening.photoHotspotHint: Each photo has one investigation point that summarises the station.
opening.photoHotspotDefault: Find the single glowing investigation point. It will summarise the fish, landmark and habitat together.
opening.hotspot.s1.fish.reaction: Wow—there used to be many blue damselfish here, in more than one group.
opening.hotspot.s1.fish.record: Several mid-water groups are visible. Abundance should only be compared against the same framing and station.
opening.hotspot.s1.station.reaction: This cable and instrument are our landmark for returning to the same view.
opening.hotspot.s1.station.record: A fixed instrument provides a spatial reference and reduces framing differences during repeat photography.
opening.hotspot.s1.habitat.reaction: The seabed is not just a background—the fish are using this habitat.
opening.hotspot.s1.habitat.record: Seagrass, reef pieces and bottom structure provide shelter and feeding space, and are evidence worth comparing.
opening.hotspot.s2.raft.reaction: The second station really is beside the fish raft—the net-cage structure is unmistakable.
opening.hotspot.s2.raft.record: The raft and net cage define this station. Today's framing should retain the same structure as a location reference.
opening.hotspot.s2.fish.reaction: The fish are not lined up; some are hidden around the cage.
opening.hotspot.s2.fish.record: Visible abundance changes with occlusion, light and movement, so repeat observations matter more than one frame.
opening.hotspot.s2.station.reaction: This monitor sits close to the raft, where water conditions may change quickly.
opening.hotspot.s2.station.record: A station near aquaculture needs repeated measurements to separate tides, operations and possible low-oxygen events.
opening.hotspot.s3.seabed.reaction: The inner-bay clue is really on the bottom, where sea cucumbers and other benthic life belong.
opening.hotspot.s3.seabed.record: Benthic organisms and bottom structure suit fixed-point comparison. Sea cucumbers should stay in contact with the seabed.
opening.hotspot.s3.station.reaction: The instrument reaches the seabed, and this third station is shallower than the others.
opening.hotspot.s3.station.record: Measurements from different depths cannot be merged blindly; instrument height and seabed position both matter.
opening.hotspot.s3.fish.reaction: There are not many fish in this photo, which reminds me to read the whole habitat.
opening.hotspot.s3.fish.record: Few fish in one frame does not mean a population vanished. Trend claims need repeated views at the same place and time.
opening.hotspot.s1.summary.reaction: Wow—the bay entrance used to show more than one fish group, with the cable and seabed clearly visible too.
opening.hotspot.s1.summary.record: Match the fixed instrument, fish groups and seabed habitat before comparing relative abundance.
opening.hotspot.s2.summary.reaction: This station is beside the fish raft; the cage, fish and instrument all help us recover the same viewpoint.
opening.hotspot.s2.summary.record: Fish may hide behind the cage or leave the frame, so keep the raft as a landmark and repeat the observation over time.
opening.hotspot.s3.summary.reaction: The inner-bay clue is on the seabed: sea cucumbers, benthic life and instrument position matter more than a distant fish.
opening.hotspot.s3.summary.record: Benthic life stays on the seabed and depth must be recorded. Few fish in one frame does not prove a population vanished.

opening.videoMutedHint: The opening is playing; click once to enable narration

lab.title: Turn one observation into a monitoring method
lab.subtitle: Read the evidence, learn the sensing principle, then plan a deployment.
lab.introTitle: Use a limited budget to find a low-oxygen event that one survey could miss
lab.introBody: Step: visit the three glowing workstations in order and press E when close.
lab.introStepEvidence:
READ EVIDENCE
Find missing time, location and depth
lab.introStepPrinciple:
RUN AN EXPERIMENT
Learn how the sensing film reads DO
lab.introStepBudget:
MAKE A CHOICE
Keep purchase and maintenance fees within budget
lab.introControls: Tip: click a workstation to let the scientist approach, or walk with A / D or the arrow keys.
lab.taskGuideControl: Tip: read the short prompt, then drag or click the glowing parts.
lab.taskGuideEvidenceTitle: TASK 1 · Find what one survey is missing
lab.taskGuideEvidenceBody: Step: read the three evidence cards, then drag continuous time, multiple locations and multiple depths to the correct gaps.
lab.taskGuidePrincipleTitle: TASK 2 · Build the DO measurement principle
lab.taskGuidePrincipleBody: Step: insert the film, let light shine on it, then use the reader to record the change. This is a principle model, not a product teardown.
lab.taskGuideBudgetTitle: TASK 3 · Design a network within budget
lab.taskGuideBudgetBody: Step: choose a device, then click a circle in the sea profile. Tip: compare purchase cost, maintenance, location, depth and continuous coverage.
lab.controls: A / D or ← / → to walk  ·  E to interact  ·  click a station to approach and interact  ·  ESC to return
lab.interact: Press E or click the workstation
lab.bubbleEvidence: The photos matter, but which monitoring dimensions are missing?
lab.bubbleEvidenceDone: The research question is ready. Try the central workbench.
lab.bubbleWorkbenchLocked: Read the evidence first so we know what to build.
lab.bubbleWorkbench: Combine the sensing film, light source and reader.
lab.bubbleWorkbenchDone: The node works. Now decide where it should go.
lab.bubbleConsoleLocked: The console cannot use the new node until the experiment is complete.
lab.bubbleConsole: Deploy equipment in the section, then run a full day.
lab.lockedEvidenceFirst: Review the evidence table on the left first.
lab.lockedWorkbenchFirst: Complete the workbench experiment to unlock a sensing node.
lab.evidenceTitle: Chapter 1 showed a change, but not its cause
lab.evidenceBody: Step: drag each missing monitoring dimension onto the evidence it completes.
lab.evidenceSampleLocation:
RECORD: Station 2
Only one fixed location
lab.evidenceSampleDepth:
RECORD: Surface 5.8 mg/L
No near-bed data
lab.evidenceTray: SURVEY TAGS · DRAG TO THE EVIDENCE GAPS
lab.evidenceDragHint: Tip: each record is incomplete in a different way. Read the clue before dragging.
lab.evidenceWrong: That dimension does not match this record. Check its clue again.
lab.evidenceComplete: All gaps completed: monitoring must span time, location and depth.
lab.evidenceTime:
TIME
One reading misses day/night, tides and short events.
lab.evidenceLocation:
PLACE
Bay entrance, raft edge and inner bay are not interchangeable.
lab.evidenceDepth:
DEPTH
A normal surface value does not guarantee the seabed is normal.
lab.experimentTitle: Build the sensing-film DO measurement flow
lab.experimentBody: Step: insert the film, let light shine on it, then read the optical change and save it. This is a principle model, not a product teardown.
lab.scienceNote: DO is oxygen in seawater that organisms can breathe. Teaching simulation: oxygen changes the sensing film's optical signal, then the reader converts that change into DO. Real materials, calibration and performance require final technical data.
lab.unlockBody: Oxygen in water changes the film's light signal. The sensor turns that change into a number we can save and compare over time.
lab.principleFlow: Oxygen in water  →  film light changes  →  DO number  →  saved data
lab.productReference: Product appearance reference · verify against final product documentation
lab.consoleTitle: Challenge: collect the most useful DO data within budget
lab.consoleBody: Step: spend up to 3600 points, deploy at glowing locations, then run 24 hours. Tip: do not chase device count alone—use limited funds to cover more sites and depths, especially near-bed gaps.
lab.selectDevice: Selected: {name} · click a glowing point to deploy or remove
lab.insufficientBudget: Not enough budget. Remove a device or choose a lower-cost option.
lab.depthLimit: {name} cannot be deployed at this depth. Choose a suitable device.
lab.simNeedSensor: Deploy at least one device before running the scenario.
lab.simRunning: Playing tides and day/night change… watch where data appears and where gaps remain.
lab.simDetected: Success! Your budgeted network captured the early-morning near-bed low-oxygen signal and earned the survey gold badge.
lab.simMissed: Data gap: this deployment did not cover the seabed event. Add a near-bed node and try again.
lab.simComplete: Scenario complete. Colored halos mark monitored points; question marks are unobserved locations.
lab.summaryTitle: What did we learn from this investigation?
lab.summaryBody: Connect the seven clues that turn a visible change into a monitoring method.
lab.summaryCompare: Compare old and new photos from the same place and a similar angle; describe visible change first.
lab.summaryFoodWeb: Food chains connect into a food web; a change in one organism may affect others.
lab.summaryGills: Fish take oxygen from water with gills; scales are not breathing organs.
lab.summaryDo: Dissolved Oxygen (DO) is oxygen in water that aquatic organisms can use.
lab.summaryLimits: One photo or reading represents one moment and cannot prove a cause by itself.
lab.summaryNetwork: Reliable monitoring needs multiple sites, multiple depths and continuous measurements.
lab.summaryFilm: Oxygen changes the film's optical signal; a reader turns the change into saved data.
lab.finalQuizTitle: Final question: how would you complete the evidence?
lab.finalQuizBody: Connect the observation, breathing clue and monitoring method from this mission.
lab.finalQuizQuestion: Which method best checks for low oxygen near the seabed before dawn?
lab.finalQuizA: Measure surface water once in the afternoon
lab.finalQuizB: Record continuously near the seabed and compare several locations
lab.finalQuizCorrect: Correct! Continuous time, near-bed depth and multiple locations fill the gaps in a one-off survey.
lab.finalQuizTryAgain: Think again: what time and depth would one afternoon surface reading miss?
lab.previewHint: All values are gameplay placeholders and must be replaced by verified product data before public use.
dive.storyThenBody: Fish appeared in groups at three fixed places.
dive.storyTodayBody: Return to the same places and take matching photos.
report.followBreathingClue: Food web complete · follow the breathing clue
report.foodLessonTask: Drag the three cards into the upper slots in the order that energy moves.
report.foodLessonTapHint: Drag the original food source into slot 1 first.
report.foodLessonDropHint: Drop it into the currently highlighted slot.
report.foodLessonWrong: Not quite. Follow the arrows from food to eater.
report.compareSubtitle: Same places, same view: compare what is visible.
report.todayGallerySubtitle: First view today's three locations together, then answer the questions.
report.todayGalleryStep: Inspect today's photo from each fixed station.
report.todayGalleryTip: Click any photo to switch then / today; describe what is visible before guessing a cause.
report.compareFishNote: Then: fish appeared in groups · Today: only a few are visible
report.compareSeabedNote: The seabed also looks less lively in today's view
report.compareQuestion: What change appears across the three views?
report.compareCauseQuestion: Does one comparison prove why it changed?
report.compareNeedEvidence: No. It is a clue; we need more evidence.
report.compareProvesCause: Yes. One photo proves the cause.
report.compareCorrect: Correct! You found a change without guessing the cause.
report.compareTryAgain: Look at the visible fish, then remember: one photo cannot prove a cause.
report.doQuestionObserve: Watch the gills open and close as oxygen in the water moves toward them.
report.doQuestionPrompt: What do fish use to take oxygen from water?
report.doQuestionCorrect: Correct! Gills take oxygen that is dissolved in water.
report.doQuestionTryAgain: Try again: watch the fish's head when it breathes.
opening.guide.s1.title: Blue damselfish
opening.guide.s1.body: A small marine fish often seen around reefs. Old photos show several together.
opening.guide.s2.title: Spotted grouper
opening.guide.s2.body: A marine reef fish that shelters near structures and ambushes smaller animals.
opening.guide.s3.title: Silver seabream
opening.guide.s3.body: A coastal marine fish. A few fish in one frame is a clue, not proof of a population change.
